queries.query: Can I have args/flags between rootcmd and subcommand

judgements.reason: The deciding mechanism: when resolving the next subcommand, flags and their space-separated values are removed and only non-flag tokens are kept, so flags may sit between the root and the subcommand; conversely the FIRST remaining non-flag token is taken as the subcommand, so a positional arg cannot precede the subcommand name.
innerfind takes argsWOflags[0] as the next subcommand and argsMinusFirstX removes that name while preserving flag values, which is what makes interleaved flags work and stray positional args fatal.

The TraverseChildren path: flags encountered before a subcommand name are collected and parsed against that parent (c.ParseFlags(flags)) before descending, i.e. the source-defined way to have the parent's own local flags accepted between root and subcommand.
The caller-facing switch that selects the Traverse path above.
Tracked documentation of the same condition; supporting evidence only.

queries.query: How to access Persistent Flags values in init function?

judgements.reason: The Cobra-provided substitute for reading flag values in a Go init(): register the function here in init(), and Cobra runs it during Execute, after flag parsing.
The essential condition: persistent flag values only exist after ParseFlags runs inside execute(), which is long after package init() has completed - so values cannot be read at init time.
preRun() is where the OnInitialize functions actually run; execute() calls it at command.go:927, i.e. after the ParseFlags above, so those functions do see parsed values.
The set that init() registers persistent flags on (binding a package variable with e.g. StringVar), which is how the value becomes visible later.
How any command later looks a persistent flag up, climbing to the parent that declared it.

queries.query: Why does `--version` not work?

judgements.reason: The source-defined cause: the --version flag is registered only when the command's own Version field is non-empty, and not at all if a 'version' flag already exists; the -v shorthand is skipped when -v is already taken.

judgements.anchor: for back-compat, only add version flag behavior if version is defined
judgements.reason: The same condition gating the behaviour at execution time: the version branch is only taken when c.Version != "".

judgements.anchor: Version defines the version for this command
judgements.reason: States the invariant in documentation form: a non-empty Version, and no user-declared version flag, is what causes the boolean version flag to exist.

queries.query: Is it possible to handle -h and --help differently?

judgements.anchor: If c already has help flag, it will do nothing.
judgements.reason: The condition that makes it possible: Cobra adds its combined BoolP(help, h, ...) flag only when no flag named help already exists, so an application that declares its own --help (without a shorthand) and a separate -h flag keeps the two spellings as distinct flags.

The mechanism that decides the outcome: execute() short-circuits to the help path purely on the boolean value of the flag named help, which is why the default single flag makes -h and --help indistinguishable and why splitting them into two flags separates the behaviour.
Shows in Cobra's own code that a shorthand letter can already belong to a different flag than the long name being registered, so the long form and the single-letter form need not be the same flag.
The hook for customising what the help path does once it is reached.
